sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed Nov 5 at 7,354, the lowest close in its one-month window and about 5.9% below the 7,819 it started at on Oct 6. The Nasdaq 100 sits at 26,630, also at its one-month low and about 14.7% under its Oct 6 level. The VIX is at 28.2, up from 15.5 a month ago and at its window high. The Euro Stoxx 50 has held up better: 6,232, roughly flat on the month and inside its range. The week carries 57 scheduled reports across the S&P 500, Russell 1000 and core names, 33 of them on Monday, with industrials and consumer-cyclical names the largest groups.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Mon: KKR US reports into the alternative-asset-management cluster, which has a +2.9% median three-day reaction off recent prints, and OXY US reports into oil-gas, where the median is -1.0%. Mon also has CEG US in utilities (-0.5% median). Wed: TGB US reports into the copper cluster (+2.6% median). Thu: HBM US, also copper, plus BN US in alternative asset management and VST US in utilities. Monday is the heaviest day by count; Friday has only one scheduled name.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Three sectors lead the reaction table by size. Alternative asset management (+2.9% median, 6 tickers, 300 news items) and copper (+2.6%, 6 tickers, 238 news items) are small groups, so read them lightly. Mining (+2.6%, 201 tickers, 2,618 news items) has a thick news window and a much broader base. Oil-gas moves the other way at -1.0% across 33 names.
